title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 24
paragraphs: While they were there, Xerxes, after making his arrangements regarding the bodies of the dead, sent a herald to the fleet. His prior arrangements were as follows: for all those of his army lying dead at Thermopylae — and there were as many as twenty thousand in all — except for about a thousand whom he left, he dug trenches and buried them, covering them over with leaves and heaping earth on top, so that they should not be seen by the men of the fleet. Then, when the herald had crossed over to Histaia, he gathered an assembly of the whole force and spoke these words: “Allies, King Xerxes grants permission to any of you who wish, to leave your post and come to see how he fights against those most senseless men who looked to overcome the power of the king.”
